title: SkillBridge Starter Toolkit
tagline: The free toolkit two high schoolers actually used to land internships, build a network, and get ahead — no paywalls, no trials that charge you in two weeks.
intro: We built this from the inside. Every tool here is genuinely free, checked June 2026. Where "free" has a catch (like a library card) we say so. At the bottom: the "free" tools that are actually traps.

sections.title: Get real experience (when you have none yet)

items.name: Forage
items.body: free virtual job simulations from real companies; do real intern tasks in a few hours, earn a resume/LinkedIn certificate; no application, 16+.

items.name: Start your own thing
items.body: a club, project, or event at your school; "founder" beats "member" on every application; free, ungatekeepable.

items.name: Your city's Summer Youth Employment Program
items.body: many cities run paid teen summer jobs; search "[your city] summer youth employment"; free to apply, usually paid.

sections.title: Get certified (free certs you can actually list)

items.name: HubSpot Academy
items.body: free marketing/sales/content certs, a few hours each, employer-recognized; certs + exams 100% free.

items.name: freeCodeCamp
items.body: free no-paywall coding certs (web design, JavaScript, Python), real projects, shareable cert; nonprofit, no card.

items.name: Google Skillshop
items.body: free Google Ads & Analytics certs straight from Google.

items.name: LinkedIn Learning
items.body: 16,000+ courses, free with a public library card (free digital card available online in minutes), completion certs.

items.name: Khan Academy
items.body: free academics + a careers section; nonprofit.

items.name: Coursera
items.body: audit almost any university course free; cert costs money unless you apply for financial aid.

items.name: FlowCV
items.body: clean ATS-friendly resumes, unlimited watermark-free PDF downloads, no trial/card/paywall; first resume free forever.

items.name: Google Docs
items.body: simplest free option; free resume templates → PDF.

items.name: Canva
items.body: free for visual portfolios/mockups/graphics; for the actual resume use FlowCV or Docs (Canva's fancy templates can confuse application scanners).

sections.title: Find the actual jobs and internships

items.name: Indeed
items.body: biggest job board; filter part-time/entry-level for teen-friendly roles.

items.name: Named programs worth knowing
items.body: NASA High School Internships (16+), Microsoft High School Discovery Program (paid), and similar run every summer; competitive but real; search the program name + "high school."

items.name: Forage (again)
items.body: when you can't land a formal internship yet, a finished simulation is the next best resume line.

items.name: LinkedIn
items.body: free, and the highest-leverage account a high schooler can make; opportunities come through people, and this is where they are.
Pair with LinkedIn Learning above, and follow us — we post how to set up a profile that isn't empty, how to message strangers without being awkward, and how to get replies.
Zety, Resume Genius, Resume.io — cheap trial that auto-renews to ~$24–26 every four weeks; use FlowCV instead.
Rule: if a "free" tool wants a credit card before you've made anything, close the tab.

outroLead: This is the shortlist we actually recommend.
outroDiscord: New guides go out in The SkillBridge Brief.
